rules.rule: Check for urgent foot symptom conditions
rules.problem: Type, trigger and contents match the red box; every red-box item is checked for. Only weakness is the 'pallor' stand-in (see c007).

rules.rule: Check for causes of foot symptoms not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Covers tinea pedis, neuropathy, PVD, plantar fasciitis and bunion discriminators. Neuropathy items drop 'constant / worse at night'; plantar fasciitis item drops 'on starting'. Not encoded (acceptable, not 'likely' logic): the joint pre-check (page 77) and the diabetes/PVD foot-at-risk screen.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable fracture with foot symptoms
Diagnose probable acute lower limb ischaemia with foot symptoms
rules.problem: and(sudden severe rest pain, or(numbness, weakness, pallor, no pulse)) matches the page. 'Pallor' is approximated by 'White discoloration of skin' because no limb-pallor concept exists; worth a clinician's eye but not a structural error.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable critical lower limb ischaemia with foot symptoms
rules.problem: and(claudication, or(rest pain, ulcer, gangrene)) matches 'Muscle pain in legs or buttocks on exercise associated with foot pain at rest, ulcer or gangrene on foot'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable tinea pedis from foot skin changes
rules.problem: or over interdigital cracks/peeling/scale and (thick and scaly) at sole/heel/border is a faithful reading of 'cracks/peeling/scaly lesions between toes or thickened scaly skin on soles/heels/sides of feet'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable peripheral neuropathy from foot symptoms
rules.problem: Probable neuropathy fires on generalised foot pain plus any burning/pins-needles/numbness of feet; the page requires these to be constant and worse at night. Broader than the page; no clean SNOMED qualifier, so accept or add a clinician note.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable peripheral vascular disease from foot symptoms
rules.problem: and(generalised foot pain, or(leg muscle pain, buttock muscle pain)) follows the page branch. Buttock structure is-a Lower limb structure, so the second disjunct is redundant but harmless.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable plantar fasciitis from heel pain
rules.problem: 'Pain aggravated by walking' is broader than 'worse on starting walking'; no closer concept found.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable bunion from foot deformity
rules.problem: Requires both 'Deformity of foot' and the 1st-MTP bony swelling; the page's bony lump is the deformity, so the conjunction is slightly redundant but faithful to the heading plus description.

rules.rule: Urgent: foot symptoms with fracture or limb ischaemia
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention ... Refer urgently.' Structure (and foot finding (or active fracture / ALI / CLI)) follows the house pattern.

summary: No invented or misplaced content: every condition traces to the page, all 43 concepts resolve, and the and/or structure of every rule follows the page's wording. The most consequential approximation is 'White discoloration of skin' of the lower limb standing in for ischaemic 'pallor' in the acute limb ischaemia rule, because this SNOMED release has no limb-pallor finding. The peripheral neuropathy rule and the plantar fasciitis rule are slightly broader than the page (dropping 'constant / worse at night' and 'on starting walking'); both are low severity with no obvious SNOMED fix.
